paragraphs.en: For most of history, exercise was considered good mainly for muscles and hearts. Scientists now agree that one of its most powerful effects happens in the head.
paragraphs.zh: 在历史的大部分时间里，运动被认为主要是对肌肉和心脏有益。科学家们现在一致认为，运动最强大的效果之一发生在大脑里。

paragraphs.en: Physical activity increases the flow of blood and oxygen to the brain and stimulates the release of chemicals that support the growth of new neurons, particularly in regions involved in learning and memory.
paragraphs.zh: 身体活动会增加流向大脑的血液和氧气，并促进某些化学物质的释放，这些物质支持新神经元的生长，尤其是在与学习和记忆相关的区域。

paragraphs.en: The benefits appear quickly. Studies show that a single walk can improve attention and mood within minutes, while months of regular training measurably enlarge brain structures tied to memory.
paragraphs.zh: 这些益处来得很快。研究表明，仅仅一次散步就能在几分钟内改善注意力和情绪，而持续数月的规律训练则能够可测量地增大与记忆相关的大脑结构。

paragraphs.en: Exercise also protects the aging brain. Older adults who stay physically active are far less likely to develop dementia, and the effect holds even for people who carry genes that raise their risk.
paragraphs.zh: 运动还能保护衰老中的大脑。保持身体活跃的老年人患痴呆症的可能性要低得多，而且即使携带增加患病风险的基因，这一效果依然成立。

paragraphs.en: Nor does one need to run marathons. Brisk walking, gardening, even household chores count. What matters most is consistency rather than intensity.
paragraphs.zh: 人们也不需要去跑马拉松。快走、园艺甚至家务活都算数。最重要的是一以贯之，而非强度。

paragraphs.en: In an age full of expensive brain-training apps and supplements, the most reliable cognitive enhancer remains free. Put on your shoes, step outside, and walk.
paragraphs.zh: 在这个充满昂贵健脑应用和保健品的时代，最可靠的认知增强剂依然是免费的。穿上鞋子，走出门去，开始散步吧。
